content: Home Assistant ships a first-party 'MCP Client' integration supporting OAuth (Application Credentials: client id/secret) for servers that implement it, and a separate 'MCP Server' integration (HA acting as MCP server) that issues its own long-lived access tokens. Community servers (ha-mcp) document webhook auth modes including 'ha_auth' requiring HA sign-in. No evidence HA's MCP Client requires a specific streamable-http vs SSE transport beyond standard MCP; Tailscale-mediated plain streamable-http (this repo's #127 plan) should work since HA treats the network layer as opaque.
